idiom_name: Vapor Fluent @Siblings through a pivot model
implementation_notes: Fluent names the join table a pivot: a model with two @Parent relations (plus optional payload fields) is the association table, and @Siblings on each end declares the many-to-many through it with key paths to both parent relations. attach and detach write and delete pivot rows - the framework performs exactly the link insert and delete the pattern describes - while a unique constraint on the pivot's two foreign keys is what keeps associations from duplicating. The pivot being a real model is the association-entity promotion available from the start.
pitfalls: Without .unique(on: "planet_id", "tag_id") in the pivot's schema, attach can create the same relation repeatedly.
attach with method: .ifNotExists costs a lookup; the default blind insert relies on the unique constraint to reject duplicates.
Pivot rows are models with their own lifecycle: deleting an end does not necessarily delete the pivot unless the schema declares the cascade or the code detaches first.

variants.name: Core Data to-many relationships with a store-created join table
variants.implementation_notes: Core Data takes the pattern literally out of the developer's hands: declaring two to-many relationships as each other's inverse makes the SQLite store create and maintain an intermediate join table itself, and the managed object API mutates the association through generated accessors (addToTags, removeFromTags). There is no model of the link table in the object graph, so the association cannot carry payload and cannot be queried directly - which is the hidden-join-table form of the pattern with the framework as the owning mapper. Where the association needs attributes, the documented alternative is an explicit join entity with two to-one relationships.
pitfalls: The generated accessors must be used to mutate the set; assigning a plain Set through the property bypasses KVO and the store's change tracking.
Faulting: touching the to-many relationship can materialise the entire association set, so large sets need predicates or fetch limits instead of navigation.
The intermediate table is not part of the model: it cannot carry columns and its name is a store implementation detail (Z_-prefixed), so code must never address it directly.
variants.idiom_name: Core Data to-many relationships with a store-created join table
